subject: Request: scoped extended log retention for Umbrabank SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Alice Thomas <alice.thomas@umbrabank.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: procure@umbrabank.com, security@umbrabank.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Hi Michael,

We're in the midst of our annual SOC 2 readiness run and our auditors have flagged a gap: for a small subset of production tenants we need session-level debug traces retained for 12 months (currently you default to 30 days). The scope is highly limited — only transactions for our payments integration (tenant id prefix UMB-PAY-) and only fields A,B,C (no PII payload).

Can Redwood provide a customer-scoped retention variance for Umbrabank, plus the artifacts auditors will accept (proof of secure storage, access logs, and a proof-of-delete for when the window lapses)? Attached is a short form our legal team uses for retention exceptions.

Specific asks:
- Confirmation that a 12-month scoped retention is technically feasible and which controls would apply
- A list of artifacts you can provide to auditors (hashes, access audit trail, KMS envelope records, deletion timeline)
- Any additional compensating controls you recommend (retention encryption at rest, restricted admin access, quarterly attestation)

We'd appreciate a reply by EOD Tuesday so we can include it in our SOC evidence pack.

Thanks,
Alice Thomas
Sr. Security Manager | Umbrabank
From: michael.grant@redwood.com <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thomas <alice.thomas@umbrabank.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the form (received). Short answer: yes, we can support a limited, tenant-scoped extended retention for debug/session traces, but there are a few engineering and compliance steps we need to confirm. Looping in Naomi (Security) and Priyom (Ops) to outline the controls and deliverables; Ben on AE/Sales side for contract/term updates.

Preliminary reply to your bullets:
- Feasibility: We have a feature toggle and per-tenant retention metadata; Ops can route UMB-PAY-* to a longer TTL bucket. We'll need a small infra change to materialize the retention window and ensure KV cache eviction rules are adjusted — no code changes to customer app surface.
- Artifacts we can provide: time-stamped storage manifest (hash per file), KMS envelope metadata (key id and envelope creation time), restricted access audit logs (who/what/when), and a deletion job report (time, objects targeted, verification hashes).
- Compensating controls: we recommend envelope encryption with a customer KMS key if required, role-based access (separate admin role for retention operations), and a quarterly retention attestation signed by Redwood Security.

Naomi: can you confirm the exact list of artifacts we would be comfortable presenting to an external auditor for a 12-month scoped retention? Priyom: what is the expected lead time for enabling this in production and any SLO/latency impact I should flag to the customer?

I'll prep a short evidence checklist and attach our standard retention-exception template for your legal team.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice / team — Thanks for the details. Confirming what we can reasonably attest to for Umbrabank's auditors: 

Deliverables (final list):
- Retention scope document (tenant prefixes, data classes included/excluded) with time-window definition
- Storage manifest: daily digest CSV with object paths, SHA256 hashes, and timestamps for the scoped retention bucket (retained for the 12-month window + 30 days for verification)
- KMS envelope metadata: key ID, envelope creation times, and a reference ID we can correlate to the stored manifests (we do not hand over raw keys)
- Access audit logs: host/service principal, admin user, operation, timestamp, and presigned object accesses (redacted IPs on request)
- Deletion verification: when TTL expires we run a deletion job that produces a verification manifest with post-delete checksums (zero-length markers) and a deletion timestamp; we can provide the job run logs and manifest.

Controls & caveats:
- We will not surface application payloads or PII in the audit artifacts. If Umbrabank requires payload-level retention, we'd need a separate review.
- Encrypted at rest by default; if you require CMK (customer-managed key) we can support via our KMS integration but we need procurement sign-off and a CMK onboarding window (2–3 weeks).
- Access to the retention manifests will be provided via a limited S3 share with time-limited credentials; we recommend the customer provide a list of auditor principals who need access.

I'm attaching a sample manifest and a short diagram that shows where the scoped bucket sits in our topology. Priyom, can you confirm lead time and if this adds measurable cost to the tenant (e.g., storage + retrieval for manifests)?

Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-soc2-log-evidence-sample.txt)
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Short operational update:
- Lead time: 7 business days to wire the retention policy, add the tenant routing rule, and enable the daily manifest job in prod (assuming no CMK onboarding). If customer requests CMK, add 10 business days for key registration, policy updates, and KMS testing.
- SLO/latency: negligible impact on request latency; storage increases and manifest generation add a small background I/O load.
- Cost/estimate: incremental storage cost (~$0.02/GB-month) + manifest generation and retrieval costs. I'll produce a quick estimate after vendor confirms expected volume for UMB-PAY-* tenants.
- Security controls: manifests are written to a customer-scoped bucket with restricted ACLs; deletion jobs are audited and require two-step approval for manual deletion outside TTL.

Next steps I recommend we take today:
1) Michael / Ben: provide a short commercial addendum that indicates the scoped retention exception, term (12 months), and any price delta.
2) Umbrabank: confirm the exact tenant prefixes and the auditor principal list for access.
3) Naomi / Ops: finalize the artifact list and deliver a sample manifest to the auditor sandbox.

Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Production Systems | Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice — appreciate the quick turnaround from the team here. For contract/commercials: we can cover the scoped 12-month retention under a short addendum to the existing SOW for Umbrabank (no long-term change required). Proposed financials: monthly incremental storage pass-through + a one-time engineering enablement fee of $5,000 to cover Ops onboarding and manifest configuration. I can put a redlined addendum in DocuSign today if you confirm: (a) tenant prefixes (UMB-PAY-*), (b) acceptance that payloads remain excluded, and (c) auditor access list.

Attaching the retention exception template and a simple topology diagram for your legal/audit review. If that works, I'll generate the DocuSign and loop procurement.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachments: umbrabank_retention_request_form.pdf, scoped-retention-diagram.png)
